title: Kalman-Filter Adaptive-Beta ETF Pairs, Rolling-Percentile Entry Threshold
methodology_caveat: spread_diff P&L proxy = day-over-day change in the Kalman filter residual (model fit error), scaled by an arbitrary 0.5x notional factor -- NOT a realistic dollar-neutral P&L model of an actual pairs trade (which should size legs using beta_t at entry and price-level, not differencing the model residual itself). Diagnostic checks run: spread_diff OOS mean~0 (0.000002), std=0.0096, skew=-0.04, top-10-day contribution only 3.3% of total abs P&L -- rules out single-event luck and rules out the H515 cash-parking degeneracy (trade_frac ~24-25% of OOS days, nowhere near the BIL standalone Sharpe of 10.385). Genuinely non-degenerate result, but Sharpe 4.6-6.2 with MaxDD <2.5% is high enough that it should not be treated as production-comparable until re-built on true leg-level dollar P&L.
verdict: PARTIAL -- non-degenerate signal confirmed, but P&L proxy needs rebuilding on real dollar terms before the Sharpe number can be trusted
